Convex hull of a point cloud or surface

Source: R/vcg-convex-hull.R
vcg_convex_hull.Rd

Computes the smallest convex closed surface that contains a set of points (for a surface, its vertices), with the Quickhull implementation of the bundled VCG library or with a port of the quickhull3d library to 'C++'.

Usage

vcg_convex_hull(x, method = c("vcg", "quickhull3d"), tolerance = NA)

Arguments

x

a matrix of point coordinates with 3 columns and one row per point, or a surface (see 'Coercing Surface Inputs' below), in which case its vertices are used and its faces ignored

method

algorithm: "vcg" (default) for the Quickhull of VCG (Barber and colleagues, 1996), or "quickhull3d" for a port of the quickhull3d library, which follows Lloyd's QuickHull3D and merges neighboring faces that lie in nearly the same plane; see 'Details'

tolerance

non-negative distance, in the units of x: a point closer than this to the plane of a hull face counts as lying on the face rather than outside it. The default NA uses the method's own value: 1e-10 times the diagonal of the bounding box for "vcg", and for "quickhull3d" the rounding error of the coordinates, three times the machine precision times the sum, over the three axes, of the largest absolute coordinate. Values below that rounding error are raised to it, because below it the visibility tests contradict each other

Value

A closed triangular mesh of class 'mesh3d' with:

vb

coordinates of the hull vertices, each one exactly an input point, in the input order

it

triangular faces, ordered counter-clockwise when seen from outside (face normals point outward)

normals

area-weighted vertex normal vectors

and attribute "vertex_index": for each hull vertex, the row of x (or the vertex index of the surface) it comes from, increasing; attr(hull, "vertex_index")[hull$it] indexes the faces by input point.

Details

Both methods start from a tetrahedron of extreme points and repeatedly add the point farthest outside a face, replacing the faces that point can see. Points within tolerance of a face plane count as on the face.

The VCG implementation keeps every face a triangle, so a flat region of the hull (common for points on a voxel grid) is split into arbitrary triangles, and it relies on the tolerance alone to stay consistent under rounding. The quickhull3d method also merges neighboring faces that lie in one plane or are not convex within the tolerance into polygons, which it splits into triangles fanning out from one corner; such a fan can contain triangles of zero area when a polygon has three corners on a line.

Points that are identical, or all lie on one line or in one plane, enclose no volume and raise an error. So does a result that fails the check for a closed, consistently oriented surface, a numerical failure that a larger tolerance or the other method can avoid.

Coercing Surface Inputs

The surface objects are converted to 'mesh3d' object before applying further calculations.

When surface is a surface ieegio object, the returned mesh3d$vb contains vertices that have been left-multiplied by surface$geometry$transforms[[1]] (the first transform stored in the geometry, typically the ScannerAnat or voxel-to-world transform).

Breaking change: Earlier versions (before 0.2.6) of ravetools returned the raw surface$geometry$vertices without applying any transform, so downstream code often multiplied by surface$geometry$transforms[[1]] (or an equivalent) manually before working in world space. Such code will now double apply the transform and produce incorrect coordinates. If you previously applied a transform from surface$geometry$transforms by hand after calling a ravetools mesh function on an 'ieegio_surface', remove that manual step.

Surfaces with an empty or missing geometry$transforms list (for example, surfaces produced by ieegio's volume_to_surface, which stores an identity transform) are unaffected.

If geometry$transforms contains multiple transforms targeting different coordinate spaces, only the first one is used. Callers that need a specific target space should select and apply that transform themselves before calling ravetools mesh functions.

References

Barber CB, Dobkin DP, Huhdanpaa H (1996). The quickhull algorithm for convex hulls. ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software, 22(4), 469-483.

Lloyd JE. QuickHull3D: a robust 3D convex hull algorithm in Java. https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~lloyd/java/quickhull3d.html

Poppe M. quickhull3d: a robust quickhull implementation to find the convex hull of a set of 3D points. https://github.com/mauriciopoppe/quickhull3d

Examples


# the 8 corners of a unit cube and 100 points inside it
set.seed(1)
x <- rbind(
  as.matrix(expand.grid(0:1, 0:1, 0:1)),
  matrix(runif(300), ncol = 3)
)
hull <- vcg_convex_hull(x)

# the rows of `x` on the hull are the corners
attr(hull, "vertex_index")
#> [1] 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8

vcg_mesh_volume(hull)
#> [1] 1

if(is_not_cran()) {

data("left_hippocampus_mask")
mesh <- vcg_isosurface(left_hippocampus_mask)
hull <- vcg_convex_hull(mesh, method = "quickhull3d")

rgl_view({
  rgl_call("shade3d", mesh, col = 2)
  rgl_call("wire3d", hull, col = 3)
})

}
